sections.english: Wherever it is in agreement with nature, the ruling power within us takes a flexible approach to circumstances, always adapting itself easily to both practicality and the given event. It has no favoured material for its work, but sets out on its objects in a conditional way, turning any obstacle into material for its own use. It is like a fire mastering whatever falls into it. A small flame would be extinguished, but a bright fire rapidly claims as its own all that is heaped on it, devours it all, and leaps up yet higher in consequence.
sections.chinese: 凡与自然相应合之处，吾人内在之统摄力皆以柔韧之姿迎接际遇，恒能轻松调适自身，既合乎实际，亦顺应所临之事。其于作为之事并无偏嗜之材料，而以有条件的方式趋向其对象，将一切障碍皆转为自己所用之资。犹如火焰，征服一切落入其中之物。微焰或为所灭，而炽盛之火则迅速将一切所加于其上者据为己有，吞尽一切，由此燃得愈发高涨。

sections.english: No action should be undertaken without aim, or other than in conformity with a principle affirming the art of life.
sections.chinese: 凡有所为，必抱宗旨，必令其符合肯定生命艺术之原则。

sections.english: Men seek retreats for themselves — in the country, by the sea, in the hills — and you yourself are particularly prone to this yearning. But all this is quite unphilosophic, when it is open to you, at any time you want, to retreat into yourself. No retreat offers someone more quiet and relaxation than that into his own mind, especially if he can dip into thoughts there which put him at immediate and complete ease: and by ease I simply mean a well-ordered life. So constantly give yourself this retreat, and renew yourself. The doctrines you will visit there should be few and fundamental, sufficient at one meeting to wash away all your pain and send you back free of resentment at what you must rejoin.
sections.chinese: 世人各寻隐退之所——或于乡间，或于海滨，或于山野——你自身亦特别易生此念。然凡此种种，皆颇不哲学，因你随时可以退隐于己身之内。世间无一隐退之所，比退归己之心灵更为安宁、更为宽弛，尤其若你能沉浸于彼处之思想，令你即刻全然安然——而我所言之安然，不过是一种秩序井然之生活。故当时时予自己此等退隐，更新自己。你将访寻之教义，当寥寥而根本，一次晤对便足以涤去你所有之痛苦，并使你毫无怨怼地重返你所必须面对之一切。

sections.english: If mind is common to us all, then we have reason also in common — that which makes us rational beings. If so, then common too is the reason which dictates what we should or should not do. If so, then law too is common to us all. If so, then we are citizens. If so, we share in a constitution. If so, the universe is a kind of community. In what else could one say that the whole human race shares a common constitution? From there, then, this common city, we take our very mind, our reason, our law — from where else? Just as the earthy part of me has been derived from some earth, the watery from the next element, the air of my breath from some other source, the hot and fiery from its own origin (for nothing comes from nothing, nor returns to nothing) — so the mind also has its source.
sections.chinese: 若心灵为人人所共有，则吾辈亦共有理性——那使我们成为理性存在者之物。若是，则那规定何者当为何者不当为之理性，亦是共有的。若是，则法律亦为人人所共有。若是，则吾辈皆为公民。若是，则吾辈共享一种体制。若是，则宇宙乃某种共同体。除此之外，还能说全人类在何处共享一种共同之体制？自此，自这一共同之城邦，吾辈领受了我们之心智、我们之理性、我们之法律——复能从何处？正如我身中土性之部分源自某处之土，水性之部分源自邻近之元素，呼吸之气息源自另一来源，热与火则源自其自身之本原（因无物自虚无中生出，亦无物归于虚无）——心智亦有其源头。

sections.english: Death, just like birth, is a mystery of nature: first a combination, then a dissolution, of the same elements. Certainly no cause for shame: because nothing out of the order for an intelligent being or contrary to the principle of his constitution.
sections.chinese: 死与生一般，同属自然之奥秘：同一批元素，先为组合，后乃分解。确然无可羞惭：因此事既不逸出理性存在者之秩序，亦不与其构造之理相悖。

sections.english: With such people such an outcome is both natural and inevitable — if you wish it otherwise you are hoping that figs will no longer produce their rennet. In any case remember that in a very brief time both you and he will be dead, and shortly after not even your names will be left.
sections.chinese: 与如此之人相遇而得如此之结果，既自然亦不可免——你若愿其不然，便是在盼无花果不再泌其凝乳。无论如何，当记取：短暂岁月之内，你与他皆将死去，再过不久，连你们的名字亦不复存留。

sections.english: Remove the judgement, and you have removed the thought 'I am hurt': remove the thought 'I am hurt', and the hurt itself is removed.
sections.chinese: 去其判断，则「我受伤害」之念已去；去「我受伤害」之念，则伤害本身已去。

sections.english: What does not make a human being worse in himself cannot make his life worse either: it cannot harm him from outside or inside.
sections.chinese: 凡不能使人自身变得更坏者，亦不能使人之生命变得更坏：此事无论自外或自内，皆不能伤害他。

sections.english: The nature of the beneficial was bound to act thus.
sections.chinese: 有益者之本性，必然如此行事。

sections.english: 'All's right that happens in the world.' Examine this saying carefully, and you will find it true. I do not mean 'right' simply in the context of cause and effect, but in the sense of 'just' — as if some adjudicator were assigning dues. So keep on observing this, as you have started, and in all that you do combine doing it with being a good man, in the specific conception of 'good man'. Preserve this in every sphere of action.
sections.chinese: 「世间所发生之一切，皆是得当的。」细察此言，你将发现其真。我所言之「得当」，非仅因果关联之意，而是如某裁判官在分派所应得一般——意即「公正」。故当如你已然开始那般，继续遵从此一观察，并在你作为一切中，兼具善人之行止，以「善人」之确切涵义。于每一行动领域，皆当持守此道。

sections.english: When someone does you wrong, do not judge things as he interprets them or would like you to interpret them. Just see them as they are, in plain truth.
sections.chinese: 有人对你行事不义之时，勿以其人所解读或愿你所解读之方式来判断事物。唯以其本来面目见之，以素朴之真实。

sections.english: Always have these two principles in readiness. First, to do only what the reason inherent in kingly and judicial power prescribes for the benefit of mankind. Second, to change your ground, if in fact there is someone to correct and guide you away from some notion. But this transference must always spring from a conviction of justice or the common good: and your preferred course must be likewise, not simply for apparent pleasure or popularity.
sections.chinese: 当时时备好此二原则。其一：仅行那内在于君权与司法权中之理性为人类之福祉所规定之事。其二：若确有某人能够纠正你、引导你脱开某种成见，便变更你的立场。然此一转移必当发自对正义或公共福祉之确信：且你所偏向之路径亦必当如是一样，非仅为表面之快意或人望。

sections.english: 'Do you possess reason?' 'I do.' 'Why not use it then? With reason doing its job, what else do you want?'
sections.chinese: 「你拥有理性否？」「我确有。」「那为何不用之？理性尽其职分之际，你还有何他求？」

sections.english: You have subsisted as a part of the Whole. You will vanish into that which gave you birth: or rather you will be changed, taken up into the generative principle of the universe.
sections.chinese: 你曾作为整体之一部分而存续。你将消逝于那赋予你生命者之中：或更确切说，你将转化，被纳入宇宙之创生原理之中。

sections.english: Many grains of incense on the same altar. One falls to ash first, another later: no difference.
sections.chinese: 诸多香粒同在一祭坛之上。其一先化为灰，另一稍后而已：并无分别。

sections.english: Within ten days you will be regarded as a god by those very people who now see you as beast or baboon — if you return to your principles and the worship of Reason.
sections.chinese: 十日之内，如今视你为野兽或狒狒之人，便将视你为神明——若你复归于你的原则，复归于对理性之崇奉。

sections.english: No, you do not have thousands of years to live. Urgency is on you. While you live, while you can, become good.
sections.chinese: 不，你没有千年可活。紧迫在你身。在你还活着、还能的时候，成为善的。

sections.english: What ease of mind you gain from not looking at what your neighbour has said or done or thought, but only at your own actions, to make them just, reverential, imbued with good! So do not glance at the black characters either side, but run right on to the line: straight, not straggly.
sections.chinese: 你若不去看邻人说了什么、做了什么、想了什么，而仅关注己之行动，使之公正、虔敬、浸染善意——你将获致何等之心安！故勿左右瞥视那些晦暗之字，径直跑向底线：直道而行，不令偏斜。

sections.english: One who is all in a flutter over his subsequent fame fails to imagine that all those who remember him will very soon be dead — and he too. Then the same will be true of all successors, until the whole memory of him will be extinguished in a sequence of lamps lit and snuffed out. But suppose immortality in those who will remember you, and everlasting memory. Even so, what is that to you? And I do not simply mean that this is nothing to the dead, but to the living also what is the point of praise, other than for some practical aspect of management? As it is, you are losing the opportunity of that gift of nature which does not depend on another's word.
sections.chinese: 为身后之名而焦躁不安者，未能想见：所有记得他的人很快也将死去——他自己亦是一样。而后，代代相继者皆如此，直至关于他的一切记忆在灯烛之递相点燃与熄灭中全然消失。然而，纵使记得你的人永生不死，记忆也永远长存。即便如此，这于你又有何干？我非仅言此于死者毫无意义：于生者，赞誉之意义何在，除了在某种实用之安排层面？事实是，你正在丧失自然所赋予的、不赖他人之辞的禀赋良机。

sections.english: Everything in any way beautiful has its beauty of itself, inherent and self-sufficient: praise is no part of it. At any rate, praise does not make anything better or worse. This applies even to the popular conception of beauty, as in material things or works or art. So does the truly beautiful need anything beyond itself? No more than law, no more than truth, no more than kindness or integrity. Which of these things derives its beauty from praise, or withers under criticism? Does an emerald lose its quality if it is not praised? And what of gold, ivory, purple, a lyre, a dagger, a flower, a bush?
sections.chinese: 一切在某种意义上是美的东西，其美皆在于自身，内在而自足：赞誉并非其组成部分。无论如何，赞誉不能使任何事物变得更好或更坏。此理甚至适用于通行的美之观念，如物质对象或艺术作品。那么，真正之美还需要自身之外的任何东西吗？不多于法律，不多于真理，不多于仁慈或正直。此等事物中，何者因赞誉而得其美，或因批评而凋萎？一颗祖母绿若无人称赞，便失其品质乎？金、象牙、紫袍、竖琴、匕首、一朵花、一丛灌木，复又如何？

sections.english: You may ask how, if souls live on, the air can accommodate them all from the beginning of time. Well, how does the earth accommodate all those bodies buried in it over the same eternity? Just as here on earth, once bodies have kept their residence for whatever time, their change and decomposition makes room for other bodies, so it is with souls migrated to the air. They continue for a time, then change, dissolve, and take fire as they are assumed into the generative principle of the Whole: in this way they make room for successive residents.
sections.chinese: 你或许会问：若灵魂继续存活，那空气何以能自时间肇始以来容纳如此众多的灵魂？好，那么大地又是如何容纳那同样永恒以来葬于其中的众多躯体？正如在地面之上，躯体居留随心之时日后，其变化与分解便为其他躯体腾出了空间，移居于空气中之灵魂亦是如此。它们存续一时，然后变化、分解、燃烧，被纳入宇宙整体之创生原理：如此这般，它们为后来之居者腾出了空间。

sections.english: No wandering. In every impulse, give what is right: in every thought, stick to what is certain.
sections.chinese: 勿再游荡。每一冲动中，给出正当之物；每一思想中，坚守确实之物。

sections.english: Universe, your harmony is my harmony: nothing in your good time is too early or too late for me. Nature, all that your seasons bring is fruit to me: all comes from you, exists in you, returns to you. The poet says, 'Dear city of Cecrops': will you not say, 'Dear city of Zeus'?
sections.chinese: 宇宙，你的和谐即是我的和谐：在你恰当之时令中，无一物于我太早或太迟。自然，你的季节所带来之一切皆为我之果实：一切自你而来，存于你中，归于你中。诗人说「亲爱的刻克洛普斯之城」：你岂不能说「亲爱的宙斯之城」？

sections.english: 'If you want to be happy', says Democritus, 'do little.' May it not be better to do what is necessary, what the reason of a naturally social being demands, and the way reason demands it done? This brings the happiness both of right action and of little action. Most of what we say and do is unnecessary: remove the superfluity, and you will have more time and less bother. So in every case one should prompt oneself: 'Is this, or is it not, something necessary?' And the removal of the unnecessary should apply not only to actions but to thoughts also: then no redundant actions either will follow.
sections.chinese: 德谟克利特说：「你若想快乐，便做少些。」岂非更好的乃是：做必要之事——即那作为天生社会性存在者之理性所要求之事，并依理性所要求的方式去做？这既带来了正确行动之乐，也带来了行动不多之乐。吾辈所言所行，多半皆非必要：去除多余，你将获更多时间，更少烦恼。故在每一情形下，人当自问：「此事是必要的，抑或不是？」而去除不必要之事，不仅应用于行动，亦当应用于思想：如此，则多余的举动亦不会随之而来。

sections.english: Try out too how the life of the good man goes for you — the man content with his dispensation from the Whole, and satisfied in his own just action and kind disposition.
sections.chinese: 也不妨一试善人之活法于你如何——那种满足于整体所分配于己之一切，并在一己之公正行动与仁厚性情中获得满足的人的生活。

sections.english: You have seen that: now look at this. Do not trouble yourself, keep yourself simple. Someone does wrong? He does wrong to himself. Has something happened to you? Fine. All that happens has been fated by the Whole from the beginning and spun for your own destiny. In sum, life is short: make your gain from the present moment with right reason and justice. Keep sober and relaxed.
sections.chinese: 你已见彼：现在看此。勿自扰扰，保持简单。有人行不义？他乃行不义于己身。有某事临到你？善。凡所发生，皆为整体自太初所注定，并为你的命运所纺成。一言蔽之，生命短促：以正确理性与公正，从当下此刻获益。保持清醒与从容。

sections.english: Either an ordered universe, or a stew of mixed ingredients, yet still coherent order. Otherwise how could a sort of private order subsist within you, if there is disorder in the Whole? Especially given that all things, distinct as they are, nevertheless permeate and respond to each other.
sections.chinese: 要么是秩序井然的宇宙，要么是由混杂原料般搅和而成、却仍具某种连贯秩序之物。否则，若整体中是混乱，一种内在之秩序又如何能在你身内存在？尤其众物虽彼此殊异，却相互渗透、相互应和。

sections.english: A black character, an effeminate, unbending character, the character of a brute or dumb animal: infantile, stupid, fraudulent, coarse, mercenary, despotic.
sections.chinese: 阴暗之品性、柔弱之品性、顽固之品性——犹如野兽或哑畜之品性：幼稚、愚蠢、欺诈、粗俗、唯利是图、暴虐专横。

sections.english: If one who does not recognize the contents of the universe is a stranger in it, no less a stranger is the one who fails to recognize what happens in it. He is a fugitive if he runs away from social principle; blind, if he shuts the eye of the mind; a beggar, if he depends on others and does not possess within him all he needs for life; a tumour on the universe, if he stands aside and separates himself from the principle of our common nature in disaffection with his lot (for it is nature which brings this about, just as it brought you about too); a social splinter, if he splits his own soul away from the soul of all rational beings, which is a unity.
sections.chinese: 若有人不识宇宙之内容而为其间之异乡人，那么不识其间所发生之事者，亦同样是异乡人。逃离社会原则者，是逃犯；闭上心灵之眼者，是盲人；依赖他人、不于自身内怀具生命所需一切者，是乞丐；远离并因对自己遭际之不满而将自己与吾辈共同自然之原则分离开来者，是宇宙上之肿囊（因正是自然带来了这些遭际，正如她带来了你一样）；将自己的灵魂从那统一整体的理性存在者之灵魂中分裂开来者，是社会之碎片。

sections.english: One philosopher has no shirt, one has no book. Here is another half-naked: 'I have no bread', he says, 'but I am faithful to Reason.' But I for my part have all the food of learning, and yet I am not faithful.
sections.chinese: 一位哲学家无衣遮体，一位无书可读。此处更有一位半裸之人：「我没有面包，」他说，「然我忠于理性。」然而就我而言，我满有学问之一切食粮，却未曾忠心。

sections.english: Love the art which you have learnt, and take comfort in it. Go through the remainder of your life in sincere commitment of all your being to the gods, and never making yourself tyrant or slave to any man.
sections.chinese: 爱你所学得的技艺，并从中得安慰。度过余生，以你全副生命真诚委身于诸神，且永勿使自己成为任何人的暴君或奴隶。

sections.english: Consider, for example, the time of Vespasian. You will see everything the same. People marrying, having children, falling ill, dying, fighting, feasting, trading, farming, flattering, pushing, suspecting, plotting, praying for the death of others, grumbling at their lot, falling in love, storing up wealth, longing for consulships and kingships. And now that life of theirs is gone, vanished. Pass on again to the time of Trajan. Again, everything the same. That life too is dead. Similarly, look at the histories of other eras and indeed whole nations, and see how many lives of striving met with a quick fall and resolution into the elements.
sections.chinese: 试想，譬如韦斯巴芗之时代。你眼前将见一切皆同。人们婚嫁、育子、患病、死亡、交战、宴饮、交易、耕作、谄媚、钻营、猜忌、图谋、祈愿他人早死、抱怨自身命运、坠入情网、囤积财富、渴望执政官与王座。而今，他们那一切生活已去，杳然无踪。再转到图拉真之时代。复次，一切皆同。彼等生命亦已死去。同样，审阅其他时代、乃至整个整个民族的史记，看看多少奋力拼搏的生命转眼间坠落，消解为元素之中。

sections.english: Words in common use long ago are obsolete now. So too the names of those once famed are in a sense obsolete — Camillus, Caeso, Volesus, Dentatus; a little later Scipio and Cato, then Augustus too, then Hadrian and Antoninus. All things fade and quickly turn to myth: quickly too utter oblivion drowns them. And I am talking of those who shone with some wonderful brilliance: the rest, once they have breathed their last, are immediately 'beyond sight, beyond knowledge'. But what in any case is everlasting memory? Utter emptiness. So where should a man direct his endeavour? Here only — a right mind, action for the common good, speech incapable of lies, a disposition to welcome all that happens as necessary, intelligible, flowing from an equally intelligible spring of origin.
sections.chinese: 往昔通行之辞语如今已废。同样，那些曾经煊赫一时之人名，在某种意义上亦已作废——卡米卢斯、凯索、沃莱苏斯、登塔图斯；稍后则有西庇阿与加图，然后是奥古斯都，再后是哈德良与安东尼努斯。一切皆褪色，迅速化为传说：然后彻底的遗忘迅即淹没它们。我所讲的还是那些曾以某种璀璨光芒闪耀过的人：其余人等，一旦咽下最后一口气，当即「不在视线之中，不在知见之内」。然而，所谓永恒的记忆究竟是什么呢？全然虚空。那么，人该将努力指向何处？唯此一处——正确之心灵、为社会公益之行动、无谎言之言语、一种欢迎一切所发生之事如必然、如可解、如自一同样可解之元始源泉中流出之性情。

sections.english: Gladly surrender yourself to Clotho: let her spin your thread into whatever web she wills.
sections.chinese: 欣然地把自己交给克洛托吧：让她将你的生命之线纺入她所乐意的任何织物中去。

sections.english: All is ephemeral, both memory and the object of memory.
sections.chinese: 一切皆朝生暮死，记忆如此，被记忆者亦如此。

sections.english: Constantly observe all that comes about through change, and habituate yourself to the thought that the nature of the Whole loves nothing so much as to change one form of existence into another, similar but new. All that exists is in a sense the seed of its successor: but your concept of 'seed' is simply what is put into the earth or the womb — that is very unphilosophic thinking.
sections.chinese: 恒常观察一切通过变化而生起之物，并令自己习惯于如下思想：宇宙整体之自然，最爱之事莫过于将存在之一种形式变换为另一种，相似然而是新的。一切存在之物，在某种意义上皆为其后继者之种子：然而你所理解的「种子」仅为投入泥土或子宫者——那是极不哲学的思考。

sections.english: Your death will soon be on you: and you are not yet clear-minded, or untroubled, or free from the fear of external harm, or kindly to all people, or convinced that justice of action is the only wisdom.
sections.chinese: 死亡很快便会临到你身：而你尚未清明，尚未安宁，尚未摆脱对外在伤害之恐惧，尚未对所有人怀仁善之心，尚未确信行动之公正即是唯一之智慧。

sections.english: Look into their directing minds: observe what even the wise will avoid or pursue.
sections.chinese: 察视那些主导之心灵：观察即便是智者，其所当避与所当追者为何。

sections.english: Harm to you cannot subsist in another's directing mind, nor indeed in any turn or change of circumstance. Where, then? In that part of you which judges harm. So no such judgement, and all is well. Even if what is closest to it, your own body, is subjected to knife or cautery, or left to suppurate or mortify, even so that faculty in you which judges these things should stay untroubled. That is, it should assess nothing either bad or good which can happen equally to the bad man or the good: because what can happen to a man irrespective of his life's conformity to nature is not of itself either in accordance with nature or contrary to it.
sections.chinese: 于你之伤害，不能存在于他人之主导心灵中，亦不能存在于任何环境之转变或变化中。那么，存在于何处？在你那判断伤害的那一部分中。故不作如是判断，一切便安然。即使那与之最为切近者——你自己的身体——遭受刀割或烙灼，或任其化脓或枯死，纵然如此，你身中判断此等事之官能也应保持不为所扰。也就是说，它不应将那些可同等降临于恶人与善人之事，判为恶或善：因为能够不加分别地发生在一个人身上的事——不论他的生命是否符合自然——其本身既非符合自然，亦非违背自然。

sections.english: Think always of the universe as one living creature, comprising one substance and one soul: how all is absorbed into this one consciousness; how a single impulse governs all its actions; how all things collaborate in all that happens; the very web and mesh of it all.
sections.chinese: 恒将宇宙思为一活物，由一实体与一灵魂所构成：一切如何被摄入此一意识之中；单一之冲动如何统摄其所有之行动；万物如何在所发生之一切中协和共作；那正是这一切之经纬与网络。

sections.english: You are a soul carrying a corpse, as Epictetus used to say.
sections.chinese: 你是一个携带着一具死尸的灵魂，如爱比克泰德常言。

sections.english: Change: nothing inherently bad in the process, nothing inherently good in the result.
sections.chinese: 变化：过程之中无固有之恶，结果之中亦无固有之善。

sections.english: There is a river of creation, and time is a violent stream. As soon as one thing comes into sight, it is swept past and another is carried down: it too will be taken on its way.
sections.chinese: 有创造之河，时间则是一条湍急之流。一物方入眼帘，便被冲卷而过，另一物又被挟裹而下：此物亦将被带走于其路途之上。

sections.english: All that happens is as habitual and familiar as roses in spring and fruit in the summer. True too of disease, death, defamation, and conspiracy — and all that delights or gives pain to fools.
sections.chinese: 一切所发生者，其惯常与熟悉正如春之玫瑰、夏之果实。疾病、死亡、诽谤、阴谋——以及一切令愚人快乐或痛苦之物，也莫不如此。

sections.english: What comes after is always in affinity to what went before. Not some simple enumeration of disparate things and a merely necessary sequence, but a rational connection: and just as existing things are harmoniously interconnected, so the processes of becoming exhibit no mere succession, but a wonderfully inherent affinity.
sections.chinese: 后来之物总是与先前之物相亲相近。并非简单一个杂多事物之罗列，亦非仅仅是必然之前后序列，而是一种理性的联结：且正如存有之物和谐地彼此相连，那生成过程所展示的也非仅是先后接续，而是一种令人惊叹的内在亲和。

sections.english: Always remember Heraclitus: 'The death of earth is the birth of water; the death of water is the birth of air; the death of air is fire, and back again.' Remember too his image of the man who forgets his way home; his saying that men are at odds with their most constant companion, the Reason which governs all things; that their everyday experience takes them by surprise; that we must not act or speak as if asleep, and sleep brings the illusion of speech and action; and that we should not be like children with their parents, simply accepting what we are told.
sections.chinese: 当时时铭记赫拉克利特：「土之死是水之生；水之死是气之生；气之死是火，复又循环。」也铭记他那个忘记归家之路的人的比喻；他所说的：人与他们最为恒常之伴侣——那统御万物的理性——相抵牾；人对他们日常之经验，总是猝不及防；我们不应如在梦中一般行动或言说，而睡眠所带来的不过是言说与行动之幻象；以及：我们不应像孩童对父母那般，简单地接受被告知的一切。

sections.english: Just as if a god told you that you would die tomorrow or at least the day after tomorrow, you would attach no importance to the difference of one day, unless you are a complete coward (such is the tiny gap of time): so you should think there no great difference between life to the umpteenth year and life to tomorrow.
sections.chinese: 正如若有神明告你，你将于明日或至少后日死去，你不会把这一日之差看作有何紧要——除非你是个彻头彻尾之懦夫（时距之微，不过若此）：同样，你当思活到某遥远年岁与活到明日，并无大异。

sections.english: Think constantly how many doctors have died, after knitting their brows over their own patients; how many astrologers, after predicting the deaths of others, as if death were something important; how many philosophers, after endless deliberation on death or immortality; how many heroes, after the many others they killed; how many tyrants, after using their power over men's lives with monstrous insolence, as if they themselves were immortal. Think too how many whole cities have 'died' — Helice, Pompeii, Herculaneum, innumerable others. Go over now all those you have known yourself, one after the other: one man follows a friend's funeral and is then laid out himself, then another follows him — and all in a brief space of time. The conclusion of this? You should always look on human life as short and cheap. Yesterday sperm: tomorrow a mummy or ashes.
sections.chinese: 请恒常思忖：多少医者在对己之病患皱眉凝思之后，自己便死去了；多少占星家在预言了他人之死亡——彷佛死亡是桩大事——之后，自己也面临了命定之日；多少哲学家在对死亡与不朽作了无尽之思辨之后；多少英雄在杀了众多他人之后；多少暴君在以可怖的傲慢运用其对人之生命权柄、彷佛自己永生不死之后。也请想想多少整座城邦已「死」——赫利刻、庞贝、赫库兰尼姆，以及无数其他。如今，再逐一回想你自己所知之人：一人参加友人之葬仪，随后自己亦躺在那里；另一人又随之而来——而一切不过发生在片刻之间。由此能得出何种结论？你当永视人生为短暂与不贵。昨为精液，明为木乃伊或灰烬。

sections.english: So one should pass through this tiny fragment of time in tune with nature, and leave it gladly, as an olive might fall when ripe, blessing the earth which bore it and grateful to the tree which gave it growth. Be like the rocky headland on which the waves constantly break. It stands firm, and round it the seething waters are laid to rest. 'It is my bad luck that this has happened to me.' No, you should rather say: 'It is my good luck that, although this has happened to me, I can bear it without pain, neither crushed by the present nor fearful of the future.' Because such a thing could have happened to any man, but not every man could have borne it without pain. So why see more misfortune in the event than good fortune in your ability to bear it?
sections.chinese: 故人当与自然相协调，度过这时间之微小片段，并欣然离之，犹如一颗橄榄在其成熟时坠落，祝福生出它的土地，感激赋予它生长的树木。要像那岩石之海岬，任凭波浪不断拍击。它屹立不移，四周滚沸之水便归于平静。有人叹：「此灾降于我，真是厄运。」不，你更当说：「此灾虽降于我，我却能安然承受，不为当下所摧，亦不畏惧将来——这正是好运。」因这样的事可发生在任何人身上，但并非人人皆能安然承受。因此，为何要在事件中见出更多不幸，而不在你承受之能力中见出更多好运？

sections.english: An unphilosophic but nonetheless effective help to putting death in its place is to run over the list of those who have clung long to life. What did they gain over the untimely dead? At any rate they are all in their graves by now — Caedicianus, Fabius, Julianus, Lepidus, and all others like them who took part in many funerals and then their own. In truth, the distance we have to travel is small: and we drag it out with such labour, in such poor company, in such a feeble body. No great thing, then. Look behind you at the huge gulf of time, and another infinity ahead. In this perspective what is the difference between an infant of three days and a Nestor of three generations?
sections.chinese: 一种不很哲学、但同样有效以安放死亡之死的方法，就是指历那些久久贪执生命之人。他们较之夭亡者，有何多得？无论如何，如今他们皆已在坟墓之中——凯迪奇亚努斯、法比乌斯、尤利安努斯、雷庇杜斯，以及所有类似之人，他们曾参加无数葬礼，然后自己也成为被葬者。事实上，所行之路短而又短：我们却以如此之劳苦、伴着如此糟糕之同伴、依靠如此脆弱之身体，延拖苟延。诚非大事。回顾你身后那时间之鸿渊，前瞻另一无限之无际。于此透观之下，三日之婴孩与年及三代的涅斯托耳，又有何异？

sections.english: Always run on the short road: and nature's road is short. Go then for the healthiest in all you say and do. Such a purpose releases a man from the labours of service, from all need to manage or impress.
sections.chinese: 时时常取短途而行：自然之道本即简短。那便在你一切言行之中，取最健全之路。如此目的，使人从劳役之事务中释放，从经营与取悦于人的一切必要中释放。
